correctness.rationale: For any x complement(x), the number of maximal letter-runs is 2 mod 4 or 3 mod 4 according to parity of the run count in x. The displayed candidates have exactly four runs with both interior runs singleton; they admit neither two-run antisquares of order>=2 nor three-run ones with middle run length>=2. For uniqueness, the canonical Dyck decomposition w=0u1v allows strong induction since avoiding contiguous forbidden factors is hereditary. Exhaustive cases according to semilengths a=|u|/2 and b=|v|/2 exclude every pair but those yielding the displayed candidate: forbidden explicit words 0011, 010101, 0110, 1100 and the family 0^a 10 1^a 01 or 01 G_b appear at relevant seams. Catalan count gives exactly 1/C_n. Independently generated all C_n Dyck words at n=1..10 and enumerated every factor/order>=2, finding precisely the stated sole word at each n. The all-n induction, not this finite check, proves the theorem.
residual_risks: Only linear contiguous factors in binary Dyck words; one-letter 01 and 10 antisquares expressly allowed.

checked_sources: Minimal antisquare classification in Baranwal et al
Catalan Dyck first-return decomposition and all-length obstruction proof
value.rationale: The precise interaction of two well-motivated languages, balanced Catalan paths and forbidden binary complement squares, collapses an exponentially large Catalan class to exactly one explicitly described word of each semilength. This exact all-length structural classification is more informative than small checks and supplies a reusable strong restriction for Dyck pattern-avoidance constructions. It need not imply a deeper theorem to qualify.
residual_risks: The unique survivor and OGF are elementary once the structural induction is found; no claim of broad consequences or generalization.

limitations: Linear binary Dyck words only; contiguous antisquares order>=2 forbidden, order-one permitted.
Counting formula 1/C_n directly follows from one-per-n classification; not independently novel.
